spec.title: Accepted rate (202) per run
spec.description: Accepted requests per second, one line per run (testid = k2-<config>-n<repeat>). The offered rate is a constant 4,000 req/s below the knee, so lines should sit at 4,000 for every config. A config that falls below 4,000 has hit its own ceiling (surprising for a mild setting). k6 series are not marked stale, so the last value lingers for minutes after a run.

spec.title: Latency seen by k6: p50 and p99
spec.description: Client-side latency per run. Look for: p50 rising with the batch wait (1 ms < 5 ms < 20 ms), acks=all above acks=1 above acks=0, and compression adding a little. Surprising: p99 far above p50 in a quiet config (a stall, not a setting). Native histogram of k6.

spec.title: Latency seen by the server (p50, p99)
spec.description: Server-side request time on POST /v1/events (includes the wait for the Kafka ack). Compare with the k6 panel: the gap is network, queueing in the accept queue and k6 itself. Server series have no config label, so read the steps over time and match them with the run times in runs.tsv.

spec.title: Average batch size (messages)
spec.description: Messages per Kafka send. At 4,000 req/s a batch holds about rate x (wait + send time): about 4 at 1 ms, 20-30 at 5 ms, 80+ at 20 ms. The size caps (50, 500, 5000) only bite when they are below that number; 500 and 5000 should look the same here. Surprising: batches near the cap at 1 ms.

spec.title: Flushes per second by reason
spec.description: Why a batch was sent: time (wait expired), size (message cap), bytes (byte cap), drain. A size cap of 50 at 20 ms should show reason=size; the rest should be reason=time.

spec.title: Average batch size (bytes, uncompressed)
spec.description: Bytes handed to the producer per batch, before compression. Expect about 500 B x the message count.

spec.title: Time in the batcher queue (p50, p99)
spec.description: Per message: from enqueue to its batch being sent. This is where the wait setting shows up directly: p99 about equal to the wait plus the previous send time.

spec.title: Time inside Kafka send (p50, p99)
spec.description: producer.send duration per batch = ack latency. Expect acks=all (idempotent or not) above acks=1 above acks=0 (which does not wait for the broker at all). Surprising: acks=1 equal to acks=all (the replicas answer faster than I think).

spec.title: Bytes sent to brokers per second (wire)
spec.description: ep_kafka_client_tx_bytes_total, added by K2 from librdkafka statistics (tx_bytes, after compression, updated every 5 s so the line is stepped). Uncompressed is about 4,000 x 600 B = 2.4 MB/s; compression should cut it. It counts only what the producer sends, not replication between brokers (that is about twice this on top).

spec.title: Wire bytes per acknowledged message
spec.description: Wire bytes divided by messages acked. The cleanest compression-ratio view: none = about 600 B, then the ratio of each codec. 1 m window because the stats arrive every 5 s. Includes protocol framing, so small batches look worse (the 1 ms configs).

spec.title: Broker round trip per broker (p99)
spec.description: librdkafka's own round trip per broker (p99 over its 5 s stats window). Shows whether one broker is slow; with acks=0 it still measures the request round trip.

spec.title: Node process CPU (user, system)
spec.description: Cores used by the whole ingest-api process (max 2.0, it is pinned to 2 logical CPUs). Compression runs in librdkafka threads inside this process, so gzip/zstd show up here as user CPU. Surprising: system CPU growing with acks (it should be mostly syscalls and network).

spec.title: Server CPU per accepted request
spec.description: Process CPU seconds divided by messages acked: the cost of one request. This is the throughput measure of K2 (1 / cost is the single-thread capacity), because at a fixed offered rate below the knee the accepted rate is the same for every config. Per-run values are also in summary.tsv (srv_cpu_ms_per_req).

spec.title: Server cores busy (CPU 0 and 6)
spec.description: Busy share of the two server CPUs (host view, includes the SMT sibling). Above about 90% on CPU 0 the main thread is the limit.

spec.title: Broker cores busy (CPUs 1,7,2,8)
spec.description: Busy share of the CPUs the three brokers share. There is no broker exporter: this is the only broker CPU view in the measured runs. Expect low at 4,000 req/s; decompression for gzip is not needed on the broker (batches are stored as sent), but replication and the log write grow with bytes.

spec.title: Disk bytes written (host)
spec.description: Bytes written to nvme0n1 by the whole host (brokers' logs times 3 replicas, plus Prometheus). Compression should lower it in proportion. The topic's size on the broker per run is also in summary.tsv (log_B_per_rec).

spec.title: Event loop lag p99
spec.description: Main-thread saturation. Surprising: more than 20 ms at 4,000 req/s (the server is near its knee for this config).

spec.title: k6 dropped iterations (must be 0)
spec.description: Requests k6 could not start. Must be 0: otherwise the run did not offer the full rate and its latency is not comparable.

spec.title: Generator cores busy (keep under 70%)
spec.description: Busy share of the k6 CPUs (3,9,4,10). Keep under 70% (K1 limit). At 4,000 req/s it should be far below.

spec.title: Shedding: 503s and rejects
spec.description: 503 answers and batcher rejects by reason. Must stay 0 at 4,000 req/s. Surprising: any queue_timeout or overloaded with acks=all idempotent (the slowest config).

spec.title: Monitoring cores busy
spec.description: Busy share of the CPUs for Prometheus, Grafana and node_exporter (5,11). Disturbance check: it should not move between configs.
